The organization is a public university with several faculties. Its members hold different offices and positions, and its decisions are taken in bodies, committees and working rounds. The statements below describe how the university is run. The university leadership sets the frame and the budget, but within that frame each body decides its own matters, and the leadership rarely intervenes. Questions are treated as separate from each other: a decision about examinations has no bearing on appointments, a decision about laboratory equipment none on the study programmes. Each body therefore handles one clearly delimited kind of question. Every member of the university has one place where their matters are decided and takes part there. Members do not sit in bodies that deal with other kinds of questions, even if their office is a higher one.

The organization has the following members of the university. The president leads the university, represents it externally and chairs its central bodies. The chancellor heads the central administration and is responsible for the budget and the staff. The vice president for studies is responsible for degree programmes, examinations and quality of teaching across the university. The dean leads one faculty, chairs its council and represents it towards the university leadership. The full professor holds a chair in the faculty, teaches, supervises and leads a research group. The junior professor holds a fixed-term professorship, teaches and builds up a research group. The research associate works on a doctorate, teaches a few courses and assists in research projects. The faculty administrative officer organizes examinations, timetables and records for the faculty. The elected student representative was elected by the students of the faculty to speak for them. The student is enrolled in a bachelor programme of the faculty and holds no office.

The following bodies and committees exist. The senate decides on the statutes, the structure and the strategy of the whole university. The budget planning round allocates the university's funds to faculties and central units for the coming year. The appointment committee selects the candidate for a vacant professorship and proposes the appointment. The faculty council decides on the affairs of one faculty, including its study regulations and its development plan. The study commission prepares changes to degree programmes and advises the faculty council on teaching. The examination board decides on examination matters of individual students, such as recognition of credits and appeals. The internal research funding round awards the faculty's small internal grants for research projects. The module revision working group rewrites the descriptions of the modules of one degree programme. The laboratory equipment procurement chooses the equipment for a teaching laboratory within a fixed budget. The orientation week planning plans the programme of the first week for new students.
